text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: GPU pool 'eu-west-1a-gpu-pool' reports 96% allocation and autoscaler health degraded - paging oncall. root cause suspected: sudden queue growth + autoscaler failing to add nodes. See metrics: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/autoscale?panel=pool_eu-west-1a
Jen C.: I'm on it. Seeing sustained queue depth rise in the last 6m. Latency p50 -> p95 jump 120ms -> 2.1s.
Carlos: i can help with infra. Any immediate customer impact?
Maya: yes, a few customers for eu-west are getting increased 5xx and token backpressure errors. Support Ops flagged three high-traffic tenants.
Ravin: autoscaler logs show repeated failures to provision GPU VMs: 
```
ERR provisioning failed: quotaExceeded: could not acquire GPU quota in eu-west-1a
WARN scale handler retrying backoff=30s attempt=4
ERR pool handshake timeout with resource-manager
```
Jen C.: interesting — quotaExceeded + handshake timeouts. But also notice continuous batching throughput dropped dramatically around the same time. Batching metrics show average batch size down from 48 tokens to ~6 tokens.
oncall-pager: @Jen C. you were paged for incident #2345678901
Jen C.: acknowledged. starting live mitigation. First steps: pause autoscaler rollouts, manually scale up pool to add 2 reserved nodes if cloud allows, and temporarily apply ingress throttling to protect control plane.
Carlos: trying manual scale now via infra-ctl: `infra-ctl pool scale eu-west-1a-gpu-pool --delta 2`
Carlos: infra-ctl returned: 409 conflict, handshake active. Trying fallback: open a ticket to cloud team for temporary quota bump and also checking if autoscaler goroutines are locked.
Maya: meanwhile, mitigate customer impact by routing new requests from high-traffic tenants to eu-west-1b pool via traffic-router: `routerctl route add --from tenant:org-42 --to pool:eu-west-1b` - will that cause double-cost but reduces 5xx.
Jen C.: good. Also looking at batching config rollout from 02:10 UTC. There was a config push that changed continuous_batch_window from 16ms to 2ms and prefix_cache_ttl from 5m -> 30s. That explains both tiny batches and cache churn leading to many prefix cache misses.
Ravin: who pushed that? config change id cfg-2024-11-09-769.
Maya: cfg-2024-11-09-769 was part of the low-latency experiment. It was rolled out to eu-west as a canary then promoted. Ops: can we rollback to previous config?
Carlos: attempt rollback: `configctl apply --pool eu-west-1a --file configs/continuous-batching-v2.json --rollback-to cfg-2024-10-31-421`
Carlos: rollback accepted by config service, applying.
incident-bot: Deploy event: config rollback triggered by Carlos at 2345679055.
Jen C.: while rollback propagates, flush prefix cache on serving nodes to avoid using stale small-ttl entries that cause cold main cache loads. Command: `servingctl cache flush --pool eu-west-1a --prefix pre-*`
Ravin: running flush now. Also temporarily increase batch window without full rollout to buy time: `configctl set --pool eu-west-1a continuous_batch_window=24ms` (local override).
Maya: traffic-router change completed for org-42 to eu-west-1b. Support Ops: ping customers we routed to verify behavior.
Support Ops: emailed affected customers with status, mitigation, and ETA for full fix (we expect rollback to finish within 4-6 minutes).
Carlos: cloud responded — quota increase in progress but provisioning still failing due to handshake timeouts with resource-manager. We're seeing a hotlock in autoscaler leader election — leader attempted to write lock and got stuck. logs: 
```
WARN leader write lock timeout: attempt=1 duration=15s
ERR failed to acquire leader lock: context deadline exceeded
```
Jen C.: ok add to action list: (1) complete config rollback, (2) flush prefix caches, (3) increase manual pool capacity if cloud quota allows, (4) restart autoscaler leader on one replica to break the lock, (5) monitor queue depth and error rate.
Ravin: restarting autoscaler process on autoscaler-0 now: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/autoscaler -l replica=0`
Ravin: restart successful, new leader elected. Leader checkout shows healthy.
incident-bot: Pager duty acknowledged by Ravin at 2345679140.
Jen C.: metrics after rollback/flush/restart: batch size climbing back to ~40, prefix cache hit rate rising from 22% -> 78%, queue depth starting to trend down.
Maya: manual scale completed: +2 nodes added to eu-west-1a at 2345679160. Pool allocation 74%.
Support Ops: 5xx rate for impacted tenants down from 4.3% -> 0.6% in the last 3 minutes. Oncall, we should leave traffic routing to eu-west-1b for 20 minutes while we monitor.
Carlos: open PR to add safety guard in config rollout pipeline to prevent continuous_batch_window < 8ms on pool-level by default. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/config-safety/pull/834
Jen C.: agreed. Also we should add an autoscaler health check to fail open rather than block manual provisioning during leader lock. Filing issue: INFRA-1429.
Ravin: posting post-incident notes for timeline and RCA. Short RCA: experiment lowered continuous_batch_window and prefix_cache_ttl -> increased tiny batches and cache churn -> throughput collapse -> queue growth -> autoscaler leader lock + quota problems prevented automated scale -> pool near exhaustion -> client 5xx and latency spikes.
Support Ops: Customer impact summary: ~7 high-traffic tenants in eu-west experienced increased error rate between 2345678901 and 2345679160; estimated 12k requests affected, highest SLA hits for org-42 and org-19. Notified customers and offered follow-up postmortem.
Maya: mitigation status: all steps completed, monitoring for recurrence for 30m. I'll stay on the thread until stable.
Jen C.: thank you everyone. Follow-ups: add rollout guard (Carlos), autoscaler leader health check (Ravin), add a canary metric for batch size to alert on sudden drops (Jen). Assign owners and due dates in the follow-up doc.
Support Ops: elevating incident to Sev-2 and scheduling 1:1 with affected customers tomorrow.
incident-bot: Incident 2345678901 moved to resolved state at 2345679210 (mitigations applied, metrics stable).
Jen C.: resolving here. Leaving thread open for postmortem notes.
Maya: thanks — will draft postmortem and include timeline + customer communications.
Carlos: will merge guard PR after review.
Ravin: will author autoscaler fix RFC.
Support Ops: closing customer notifications loop.
